findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` as its first argument and runs the query against it, but the upsampling decision is computed with the outer, request-level `dataset`: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)`. In the dashboard-widget split path (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is deliberately invoked with other datasets (`discover`, `split_dataset`) and with rewritten queries (`"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` / `"... AND event.type:transaction"`). Consequently (a) a transactions-only sub-query can be transformed to `upsampled_count()` when the request-level dataset is `errors`, producing a query over a dataset where `sample_weight` is not meaningful/absent, and (b) an errors-only sub-query run against `discover` will not be upsampled unless the *raw* request query string happens to contain `event.type:error`, since `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET["query"]` rather than the effective `query` passed in. The decision should be based on `scoped_dataset` and the effective query string.

findings.title: 60s cache of allowlist eligibility is unkeyed on option state and effectively uninvalidatable
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the result of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` for 60 seconds under a key built only from the organization id and a hash of the project id set. `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist")` is already a cheap, locally cached option read, so the added cache buys little while introducing a window in which counts flip between raw `count()` and upsampled `upsampled_count()` for the same dashboard/alert, i.e. visibly inconsistent numbers after an allowlist change. Worse, invalidation is impossible in practice: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 67) requires the exact project-id tuple that was queried, so a single allowlist change cannot be propagated to the unbounded set of cached project-set combinations, and the function is never called anywhere in this PR. Either drop the cache or key it on the allowlist value/version.

findings.title: Cache key uses Python `hash()` of project ids, allowing silent collisions
findings.body: The cache key is `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Different project-id sets within the same organization that collide under `hash()` will share a cache entry, so a non-allowlisted project set can be served an `is_eligible=True` verdict and have its `count()` silently multiplied by sample weights (or vice versa). Use a deterministic, collision-free key such as the sorted ids joined by a separator (or a cryptographic digest of it).

findings.title: Docstring claims fresh config reads while the caller caches for 60s
findings.body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`'s docstring states it "reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... This is intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state." The only caller caches its result for 60 seconds (line 38), so the documented behavior is the opposite of the actual behavior. A future reader relying on this comment will assume allowlist changes take effect immediately.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` with no null/zero fallback and declares a mismatched result type
findings.body: The new SnQLFunction emits `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Any error event stored without a populated `sample_weight` (events ingested before the field was written, or non-upsampled events in an allowlisted project) contributes 0 instead of 1, so `count()` queries silently under-report after the transform is applied; a `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)`-style fallback is needed, or the allowlist guarantee must be enforced elsewhere. Additionally `default_result_type="number"` contradicts the `toInt64` cast and the `"integer"` type used by the sibling count functions, so the response meta will advertise the wrong field type to clients formatting the value.

findings.title: Accidental git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: This PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` ("Subproject commit a5d2909...") with no corresponding `.gitmodules` definition. Clones and CI checkouts of such a dangling gitlink produce an empty directory and `git submodule` operations fail with "No url found for submodule path 'sentry-repo'". This is clearly unrelated to the upsampling feature and should be removed from the branch.

findings.title: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` swallows all exceptions, hiding bad test fixtures
findings.body: Both `try/except Exception: pass` blocks silently discard failures: a non-numeric `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` in a test fixture will simply not set `sample_rate`, so upsampling tests will quietly assert on un-upsampled counts instead of failing loudly on malformed input. Since `normalized_data.get("contexts", {}).get(...)` cannot realistically raise for dict data, the first `except` is dead and the second should either validate explicitly or let the error surface.

findings.title: No coverage for the `errors` dataset path or for the cached public eligibility function
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally for the `errors` snuba dataset, but every new endpoint test here goes through the default/`discover` dataset; there is no test issuing `dataset=errors` with `yAxis=count()`, so it is unverified that `upsampled_count()` (registered only in `discover.py`'s function converter) actually resolves for the errors query builder — if it does not, those requests would fail with an unknown-function error in production. Likewise, the unit test file only exercises the private helpers; the public `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, including its new 60-second cache and the cache-hit branch at line 32 of `error_upsampling.py`, is entirely untested (e.g. that a cached `False` is honored and that stale entries behave as documented).

findings.title: Trailing whitespace and duplicated transform blocks will fail lint/black
findings.body: Several added lines contain trailing whitespace (e.g. after `)` on line 223, line 234, line 278 here and in the docstrings of `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`), which `black --check` / pre-commit in this repo will reject, breaking CI. Additionally `should_upsample` is immediately aliased to `upsampling_enabled` and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is repeated in three branches; computing `final_columns` once before the branching would remove the duplication and the misleading "late transformation"/"caching" comments, which do not describe anything the code actually does.
